GHSA-CPGF-5MJF-73P7.f776f963b9d9346271aade9cb903e793fd38e865:
Scrub SVG href attributes in linear time

`PermitScrubber#scrub_attribute` tested SVG `href` and `xlink:href`
against `/^\s*[^#\s].*/m`. `^` matches every line start and `\s` includes
`\n`, so on an all-whitespace value the engine rescanned the whole run
from each of its n line starts, which is O(n²). A 20 KB attribute took
3.4 seconds on Ruby 3.1.7. Ruby 3.2's linear-time regexp matching hides
this, so only Ruby 3.1 and earlier are affected.

Call `Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.prefixed_attribute_name` and
`.scrub_attribute_value` rather than repeating loofah's attribute rules
here, which drops the pattern from this repo. `scrub_attribute_value`
returns true only when the URI scrub removed the attribute, so a
local-href removal still falls through to the `src` check and
`force_correct_attribute_escaping!` as it did before.

Require Loofah >= 2.25.3, the first release with those methods.

ref: https://github.com/rails/rails-html-sanitizer/security/advisories/GHSA-cpgf-5mjf-73p7

GHSA-9WJQ-CP2P-HRGF.74dcb8053e6da9921246ce71b06ad9fd65b19586:
Properly restrict SVG href attributes

PermitScrubber reimplements Loofah's SVG local-reference restriction,
which covered only `xlink:href`. SVG 2 also allows plain `href`, so
`<use href="https://example.com/x.svg#p"/>` passed through intact.
Restrict both via Loofah's SVG_HREF_ATTRIBUTES set (Loofah >= 2.25.2),
mirroring the related Loofah fix for GHSA-9wjq-cp2p-hrgf.

ref: https://github.com/rails/rails-html-sanitizer/security/advisories/GHSA-cj75-f6xr-r4g7

CVE-2015-7579.49dfc1584c5b8e35a4ffabf8356ba3df025e8d3f:
Do not unescape already escaped HTML entities

The full sanitizer was using Loofah's #text method that automatically
escapes HTML entities. That behavior caused some problems where strings
that were not escaped in the older sanitizer started to be escaped. To
fix these problems we used the #text's `encode_special_chars` option as
`false` that not just skipped the HTML entities escaping but unescaped
already escaped entities.

This introduced a security bug because an attacker can pass escaped HTML
tags that will not be sanitized and will be returned as unescaped HTML
tags.

To fix it properly we introduced a new scrubber that will remove all
tags and keep just the text nodes of these tags without changing how
to escape the string.

CVE-2015-7579

CVE-2015-7578.297161e29a3e11186ce4c02bf7defc088bf544d4:
